summary: On this host, proxy environment variables can turn local curl checks against published Docker ports into false 502s; force '--noproxy *' in verification scripts and direct evidence commands.
symptom: Plain curl to the published localhost port returns 502 even though the container is healthy and in-container HTTP requests return 200.
root_cause: Host-level proxy environment variables intercept local HTTP verification traffic unless curl is told to bypass the proxy.
fix: Add '--noproxy *' to all localhost verification curls.
Document the proxy caveat in final audit artifacts and quick verification guidance when needed.
precheck: If localhost checks show 502 but the container is healthy, retry the same request with '--noproxy *'.
Compare host curl with 'docker exec ... curl 127.0.0.1:<container-port>' before changing the application.
anti_pattern: Treating a proxied localhost 502 as an application failure without testing the same URL with proxy bypass.
quick_checks: Verify root and login pages with 'curl --noproxy *'.
Keep verification scripts explicit about bypassing proxy env for local ports.

summary: On this host, Forgejo HTTP git verification can fail with a false 502 when Git honors host proxy variables for localhost traffic; disable the Git HTTP proxy for local checks.
symptom: git ls-remote against the local Forgejo HTTP clone URL returns 502 even though curl to the git info/refs endpoint returns 200 and the application is healthy.
root_cause: The host environment exports http_proxy/https_proxy, and Git routes localhost HTTP clone traffic through that proxy unless its proxy config is explicitly disabled.
successful_path: Keep curl verification on localhost explicit with --noproxy '*' and run local Git protocol checks with '-c http.proxy= -c https.proxy=' so the request goes directly to the published Forgejo port.
fix: Re-run git ls-remote with '-c http.proxy= -c https.proxy=' for local Forgejo URLs.
Confirm the app endpoint directly with curl --noproxy '*' before treating Git's 502 as an application failure.
precheck: Inspect env for http_proxy/https_proxy before trusting localhost Git HTTP failures.
Compare Git behavior with a direct curl to /info/refs?service=git-upload-pack.
anti_pattern: Do not classify a proxied localhost git ls-remote failure as a Forgejo deployment regression without a direct no-proxy HTTP check.
quick_checks: curl --noproxy '*' -I 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<owner>/<repo>.git/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack' should return 200.
git -c http.proxy= -c https.proxy= ls-remote http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<owner>/<repo>.git should succeed.

summary: On this host, localhost verification for Fluent Bit's monitoring and ingest endpoints can false-fail through proxy environment handling unless curls explicitly use `--noproxy '*'`.
symptom: An evidence-capture wrapper produced false localhost `502` results even though the service was healthy and direct no-proxy curls succeeded.
root_cause: Host proxy environment variables can intercept local HTTP checks unless the verification command bypasses proxy resolution explicitly.
successful_path: Run all local monitoring and ingest verification with `curl --noproxy '*'` and, if a wrapped command reports 502, rerun the same URL directly with proxy bypass before diagnosing the application.
fix: Use `curl --noproxy '*'` in deploy, verify, and audit evidence commands against localhost ports.
Record the corrected no-proxy result in logs rather than treating proxied localhost 502s as application failures.
precheck: If a localhost Fluent Bit endpoint returns 502 unexpectedly, retry the same request with `--noproxy '*'` before changing the bundle.
Keep portable-bundle verify scripts explicit about proxy bypass for local ports.
anti_pattern: Do not classify proxied localhost 502s as a Fluent Bit regression without a direct no-proxy retest.
quick_checks: `curl --noproxy '*' http://127.0.0.1:<metrics-port>/api/v1/metrics/prometheus` returns HTTP 200.
`curl --noproxy '*' -d ... http://127.0.0.1:<ingest-port>/` returns HTTP 201.

summary: When the host exports http_proxy/https_proxy, localhost checks can produce false 502 responses unless verification forces direct access with curl --noproxy '*'.
symptom: A healthy locally published service returns HTTP 502 only during host-side verification.
root_cause: Proxy environment variables intercept localhost requests and route them through an upstream proxy instead of the local bind.
successful_path: Inspect proxy-related environment variables and rerun all localhost HTTP checks with curl --noproxy '*'.
fix: Verify whether http_proxy or https_proxy is set on the host.
Use curl --noproxy '*' for localhost and 127.0.0.1 verification commands.
Document the requirement in deploy and quickstart verification steps when it affects the current environment.
precheck: Check env for proxy variables before diagnosing localhost 502 responses as app failures.
anti_pattern: Treating a proxied localhost 502 as evidence that the container or application is broken.
Retrying deployment changes before ruling out host proxy interference.
quick_checks: env | rg 'NO_PROXY|no_proxy|HTTP_PROXY|HTTPS_PROXY|ALL_PROXY|http_proxy|https_proxy|all_proxy'
curl --noproxy '*' -I http://127.0.0.1:<port>/

summary: In single-container oCIS deployments, bearer-protected proxy routes can fail with `401` even after a successful OIDC token exchange if `OCIS_URL` points to a host-visible issuer URL that the container cannot reach on the same port.
symptom: OIDC login and `/konnect/v1/token` succeed, but bearer-authenticated `/graph/v1.0/me/drives` and `/remote.php/webdav/...` return `401 Unauthorized`.
root_cause: The proxy verifies bearer tokens by fetching the issuer metadata from `OCIS_URL`. If the configured issuer host/port is not reachable from inside the container on that same port, token verification fails even though token issuance works.
successful_path: Make `OCIS_URL` self-reachable from inside the container and align `PROXY_HTTP_ADDR` with the externally published port so the issuer URL resolves to the same live proxy listener both from the host and from inside the container.
fix: Set `OCIS_URL` to the actual verified public URL.
Set `PROXY_HTTP_ADDR` to the same internal listener port used by the issuer URL.
Publish the same container port externally so the issuer URL stays coherent across host and container verification paths.
Re-test `/konnect/v1/userinfo`, `/graph/v1.0/me/drives`, and WebDAV after the port alignment change.
precheck: Before diagnosing Graph/WebDAV auth failures, inspect proxy logs for `failed to verify access token` errors that reference `.well-known/openid-configuration`.
Check whether the container can actually reach the configured `OCIS_URL` on its own listener port.
anti_pattern: Changing only `OCIS_URL` while leaving `PROXY_HTTP_ADDR` on the old internal port.
Assuming a successful token exchange guarantees Graph and WebDAV will work without checking proxy self-reachability of the issuer URL.
quick_checks: `docker logs <ocis-container> | rg 'failed to verify access token|.well-known/openid-configuration'`
After remediation, require bearer-authenticated `GET /konnect/v1/userinfo`, `GET /graph/v1.0/me/drives`, and WebDAV PUT/GET to pass.

summary: Verdaccio's container runs as UID 10001; bind-mounted conf and storage paths that are not writable by that UID cause user creation and package persistence to fail.
symptom: PUT /-/user/org.couchdb.user:* returns 500 with EACCES, publishes fail, or npm localhost calls hang unexpectedly.
root_cause: The mounted host paths were owned or permissioned for the host user rather than container UID 10001, and npm inherited proxy variables for localhost registry access.
successful_path: Before debugging Verdaccio auth logic, verify the container can write /verdaccio/conf/htpasswd and /verdaccio/storage, fix ownership or mode for UID 10001, and run npm localhost verification with proxy variables unset.
fix: Use a root docker exec to chown/chmod mounted conf and storage for UID 10001 when host ownership blocks writes.
Unset http_proxy, https_proxy, and related variables for localhost npm commands.
precheck: Inspect docker inspect <container> --format '{{.Config.User}}' before assuming bind mounts are writable.
Test docker exec -u 10001 <container> touch /verdaccio/conf/htpasswd.test and /verdaccio/storage/testfile early.
Check environment proxy variables before treating stalled npm localhost auth calls as app failures.
anti_pattern: Do not chase npm auth configuration first when Verdaccio cannot write htpasswd or storage.
Do not trust npm localhost behavior while proxy variables are still exported.
quick_checks: docker logs <container> | rg 'EACCES|htpasswd|storage'
docker exec -u 10001 <container> sh -lc 'touch /verdaccio/conf/htpasswd.test && touch /verdaccio/storage/testfile'
env | rg 'NO_PROXY|no_proxy|HTTP_PROXY|HTTPS_PROXY|ALL_PROXY|http_proxy|https_proxy|all_proxy'

summary: Host-side localhost verification may need curl --noproxy '*' to avoid false proxy-mediated 502 responses.
symptom: HTTP checks to 127.0.0.1 can return 502 without Apache headers even though the container is healthy and direct no-proxy checks succeed.
root_cause: Host proxy environment interferes with localhost HTTP verification unless curl bypasses proxy resolution.
successful_path: Use curl --noproxy '*' for host-side runtime checks and portable bundle verification commands.
fix: Add --noproxy '*' to live verification curls and documentation snippets.
precheck: Compare response headers when localhost checks look proxied or return generic 502 responses.
anti_pattern: Treating proxy-mediated 502 responses as app failures before retrying with direct no-proxy curls.
quick_checks: Expect Apache/Flarum headers on direct checks.
If headers are missing, rerun with --noproxy '*' before remediating the app.

summary: When Docker Hub auth or manifest requests return EOF during PHP app deployment, avoid adding extra helper-image pulls if a small required tool can be fetched directly on the host and copied into the build context instead.
symptom: `docker build` or `docker pull` fails intermittently on Docker Hub auth or manifest fetches for base/helper images.
root_cause: External registry transport instability makes large or additional image pulls unreliable, even when small direct HTTPS downloads still succeed from the host.
fix: Prefer reusing already-known local base images when available.
If only a small helper binary is needed, download it on the host and copy it into the build context instead of pulling an extra helper image.
precheck: Test a small direct host-side HTTPS fetch before introducing an additional helper image pull.
Treat Docker Hub OAuth or manifest EOFs as external network evidence, not immediate application misconfiguration.
anti_pattern: Adding more Docker Hub helper-image pulls when the current failure mode is registry auth or manifest EOF.
Assuming the application configuration is broken before ruling out registry transport instability.
quick_checks: `curl --noproxy '*' -I https://getcomposer.org/download/latest-stable/composer.phar`
`docker pull <image>` and inspect whether the failure is an auth/manifest EOF rather than an image build error.

summary: For Keycloak main source builds behind a proxy, configure Git explicitly, treat isolated Maven TLS handshakes as network bootstrap issues first, and release stale port claims before bundle re-deploy verification.
symptom: Source fetch or dependency bootstrap appears broken, or Phase 6 re-deploy collides with an already claimed port even though the app logic is fine.
root_cause: Git may not inherit system proxy settings, Maven Central handshakes can fail transiently, and the shared port registry can retain the primary claim when the portable verification wants to reuse the same port.
successful_path: Set `git config --global http.proxy/https.proxy` to the working proxy, keep shell proxy envs for Maven/npm fetches, preload or retry a single failed Maven artifact instead of abandoning the source build, and release or refresh stale port claims before the portable bundle scripts reuse the selected port.
fix: Configure Git proxy explicitly before cloning or `ls-remote` checks.
Handle one-off Maven TLS handshake failures as transient fetch issues when the artifact is otherwise reachable.
Release the existing port claim before Phase 6 re-deploy if the verification scripts need to claim the same port again.
precheck: Test `git ls-remote` against the repo before assuming source access is healthy.
Check whether the chosen application port is still reserved in the shared registry before bundle re-deploy.
anti_pattern: Do not misdiagnose a single dependency handshake failure as a Keycloak source or compile defect.
Do not let Phase 6 fail on a stale registry reservation when the port is intentionally reused by the same task lineage.
quick_checks: Verify Git proxy config separately from Docker proxy config.
If exactly one Maven artifact fails handshake, confirm it is reachable before changing the build plan.
Inspect and refresh the port registry before final bundle verification.

summary: On this host, proxy environment variables can make plain localhost curl checks against LiveKit return false 502s; direct local verification should force --noproxy '*'.
symptom: Local verification appears broken with HTTP 502 even though the LiveKit container is healthy and direct checks succeed.
root_cause: Host http_proxy/https_proxy settings intercept localhost HTTP checks unless verification explicitly bypasses the proxy.
successful_path: Re-run localhost checks with curl --noproxy '*', keep Twirp and /rtc/validate verification on the direct path, and treat proxy-only failures as non-app issues.
fix: Use curl --noproxy '*' for localhost verification and audit commands.
Document the proxy caveat in audit warnings instead of remediating the app.
precheck: env | rg 'NO_PROXY|no_proxy|HTTP_PROXY|HTTPS_PROXY|ALL_PROXY|http_proxy|https_proxy|all_proxy'
Rerun any surprising localhost HTTP failure with curl --noproxy '*' before changing the deployment.
anti_pattern: Do not treat a proxy-mediated localhost 502 as evidence that the LiveKit service itself is down.
quick_checks: curl --noproxy '*' -I http://127.0.0.1:<port>/
Keep direct local Twirp and /rtc/validate checks on the no-proxy path.

summary: When http_proxy is set on the host, localhost curl checks can be routed through the proxy and falsely return 502 even while the LinOTP container serves 302/200 correctly.
symptom: Host-side GET / or /manage/ appears to fail with 502 while container health and in-container curl are good.
root_cause: curl honors the host http_proxy environment and can send localhost verification through an upstream proxy instead of directly to 127.0.0.1.
successful_path: Repeat the host-side checks with curl --noproxy '*' so verification hits the published localhost port directly.
fix: Use curl --noproxy '*' for localhost verification when proxy environment variables are present.
Cross-check with in-container curl if host-side results look inconsistent with healthy app logs.
precheck: Inspect env | rg '(^|_)http_proxy|https_proxy' before trusting a surprising localhost HTTP failure.
anti_pattern: Do not classify a localhost 502 as an application failure before ruling out proxy interception.
quick_checks: curl --noproxy '*' -sSI http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ | head
docker exec <app-container> curl -sSI http://127.0.0.1:5000/ | head

summary: On this host, Docker daemon pulls of Appsmith v1.99 can stall on large layers even when the registry is reachable; exporting the same official image with a userland registry client and then docker loading it avoids wasted retries.
symptom: docker compose up -d or docker pull repeats the same Appsmith layer byte count without progressing to completion.
root_cause: The daemon-side registry transport on this host can stall on large Appsmith layers even though direct userland HTTPS requests to the registry still work.
successful_path: If repeated pull status lines show no byte progress across checks, switch from daemon pulls to a standalone registry client export of the same official image, then docker load the tar and continue with the standard compose deployment.
fix: Watch for repeated identical byte counts in the same image layer before retrying the whole deployment.
Use regctl image export <image> <tar> --platform linux/amd64 --name <image> and then docker load -i <tar>.
Resume the official Docker compose flow unchanged once the image is loaded locally.
precheck: If Appsmith image pulls appear stuck, compare several tail samples from the deploy log and confirm the same layer byte count is repeating.
Check that direct curl access to registry-1.docker.io still works before changing the deployment plan.
anti_pattern: Blindly rerunning docker compose up against the same stalled Appsmith image pull without changing the transport path.
quick_checks: tail -n 20 DP_LOGS/<project>/deploy.log shows repeated identical layer progress for the same digest.
docker image ls shows the Appsmith image immediately after docker load, allowing compose startup to proceed without another remote pull.

summary: On this host, Apollo Rover can route localhost subgraph introspection through the configured proxy unless `NO_PROXY` and `no_proxy` explicitly include `localhost,127.0.0.1`, causing false 502 failures during local supergraph composition.
symptom: Gateway startup fails while composing the supergraph with Rover, reporting `HTTP status server error (502 Bad Gateway) for url (http://localhost:3300/graphql)` even though the core GraphQL endpoint is healthy locally.
root_cause: The host exports proxy environment variables but no matching localhost bypass, so Rover sends local subgraph introspection through the proxy path.
fix: Start the gateway with `NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1 no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1`.
Keep local verification curls explicit with `--noproxy '*'` while debugging the stack.
precheck: Inspect `http_proxy` and `https_proxy` before starting local gateway tooling that introspects localhost endpoints.
If `NO_PROXY` is absent, add `localhost,127.0.0.1` before running Rover-based startup.
anti_pattern: Treating Rover's localhost 502 as a core subgraph application failure before checking proxy bypass.
quick_checks: `curl --noproxy '*' -H 'content-type: application/json' --data '{"query":"query { __typename }"}' http://127.0.0.1:3300/graphql` should return 200 while Rover still fails without `NO_PROXY`.
Restarting gateway with explicit `NO_PROXY` should let supergraph composition complete.
evidence: Gateway startup succeeded after exporting `NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1` and `no_proxy=localhost,127.0.0.1`.

summary: During portable bundle re-deploy, a stale shared port-registry claim can survive the primary runtime teardown and falsely block reuse of the validated public port until the claim is released.
symptom: Phase 6 bundle redeploy fails before startup because the chosen public port is still marked as claimed even though the original runtime has been removed.
root_cause: The shared registry coordination layer can retain an old project claim after the primary deployment is torn down, blocking a clean bundle redeploy on the same host port.
fix: Inspect the registry claim owner when Phase 6 reports a port conflict on a recently used port.
Release the stale project claim and rerun the redeploy verification.
precheck: Before final redeploy on the same port, refresh and inspect the shared port registry state.
anti_pattern: Changing the verified public port immediately instead of checking for a stale registry claim from the primary deployment.
quick_checks: Run the port-registry show or snapshot path when the bundle redeploy reports a port claim conflict.
If the original project no longer owns a running container, release its stale claim before retrying.

summary: For ISPConfig, verify that `git.ispconfig.org` can actually return Git refs from the current runner before committing to the deployment path; on this host the connection reached TLS setup but stalled on `/info/refs`, while direct no-proxy HTTPS timed out entirely.
symptom: `git ls-remote` to the official repo hangs after the request for `/info/refs`, and direct HTTPS probes to `git.ispconfig.org` time out with no response body.
root_cause: The runner cannot reliably fetch the official ISPConfig Git host, so the official source path is unavailable even before deployment starts.
successful_path: Probe the official host with both git and direct HTTPS early; if it cannot return refs, stop and document the external source-fetch blocker instead of improvising a different upstream.
fix: Run `git ls-remote` against the official repo before cloning or planning the install path.
Cross-check with `curl --noproxy '*' -I https://git.ispconfig.org/` to distinguish proxy issues from direct reachability failure.
precheck: Use one quick Git ref probe against the target repo before building the deployment plan.
If the host uses proxies, test both proxied git and direct `--noproxy` HTTPS.
anti_pattern: Spending time on container or packaging work before confirming the official repo host can supply the target source tree.
quick_checks: `git ls-remote https://git.ispconfig.org/ispconfig/ispconfig3.git`
`curl --noproxy '*' -I https://git.ispconfig.org/`

summary: On this host, Ubuntu container APT mirrors can hang or fail during `apt-get update` while Debian bookworm package mirrors remain reachable, so mirror reachability should be tested before retrying a long source-build image path.
symptom: A Docker build based on Ubuntu stalls in `apt-get update` with repeated `Ign:` lines or mirror transport failures even though image pulls and other internet access still work.
root_cause: This environment can reach Debian mirrors but not the Ubuntu APT mirror path needed by the default Ubuntu base image sources.
fix: Probe candidate distro mirrors with a short curl or trial container run before committing to a long build.
If Ubuntu APT is blocked but Debian APT works, switch the runtime carrier to Debian while keeping the upstream application install sequence unchanged and document the deviation.
precheck: Run `curl -I --max-time 15 https://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/bookworm/InRelease` and compare it with the target Ubuntu mirror reachability.
If an Ubuntu-based build shows repeated `Ign:` entries in `apt-get update`, stop and confirm mirror reachability instead of waiting through repeated retries.
anti_pattern: Retrying the same Ubuntu-based Docker build multiple times without first validating mirror reachability or testing an alternative compatible carrier.
quick_checks: `docker run --rm debian:bookworm-slim bash -lc 'apt-get update >/tmp/apt.log 2>&1; tail -n 20 /tmp/apt.log'`
`curl -I --max-time 15 https://mirrors.ustc.edu.cn/ubuntu/dists/noble/InRelease` when Ubuntu mirror accessibility is uncertain.

summary: For Casdoor v3.52.0 on this host, official deployment attempts can fail before runtime due to artifact transport bottlenecks: Docker image pulls, frontend dependency fetches, and GitHub release tarball downloads should all be throughput-checked before committing to a path.
symptom: Official Docker, source-build, and release-artifact paths all stall for long periods while acquiring required upstream artifacts.
root_cause: Host transport performance to upstream registries and release assets is too low or unstable for the required Docker layers, npm packages, or GitHub release tarballs.
fix: Probe the official GitHub release asset and frontend package-registry throughput before starting the main deployment path.
Prefer the official prebuilt release artifact when it can be fetched at usable speed; otherwise fail early rather than waiting through repeated stalled installs.
precheck: Run a bounded ranged download against the official GitHub release tarball and confirm usable throughput before selecting the release-artifact path.
Run a bounded registry probe before committing to `yarn install` for the frontend build.
anti_pattern: Do not spend multiple deployment attempts on long-running fetch steps that show repeated retries or impractically low sustained throughput without first measuring the transport path.
quick_checks: Confirm the latest release asset URL resolves and can download at a practical rate.
Confirm frontend package fetches progress without repeated retry loops before counting on a source build.
